newsitem.title: USA: Catastrophe exchange expected to open Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Catastrophe exchange expected to open Tuesday.

text.p: An exchange that would allow customers to trade insurance risks has set up offices in New York City and was expected to launch operations on Tuesday, New York insurance regulators said.
However, officials from the Catastrophe Risk Exchange (Catex) in Princeton, N.J., did not return repeated phone calls and the launch date could not be confirmed.
Catex, which won approval from New York insurance regulators last year, would allow subscibers to swap catastrophic risk exposures over a nationwide computer system similar to a global trading room.
Catex is one of a number of new mechanisms being developed to help insurers reduce the risk of massive losses from a major catastrophe like an earthquake or hurricane.

Insurers have grown increasingly reluctant to write insurance in catastrophe-prone areas following huge losses on the U.S. East Coast from Hurricane Andrew in 1992 and on the earthquake in Northridge, Calif., in 1994.

The system would let an insurer reduce its exposure to catastrophes by allowing it to pay another company to accept some of its risk or by allowing it to give away one set of risks in return for accepting a separate bundle of risks.
Everest Reinsurance Holdings Inc in August said it had agreed to become the first subscriber to Catex, saying it believed the system had the potential to develop into a new source of business.
An Everest Re spokeswoman on Friday said the company did not know whether the exchange was ready to begin operating on Tuesday.
In addition, she said she did not know whether the exchange had signed up any more subscribers.
The system would need at least a few subscribers to allow the trading to take place, she said.
She said Everest Re expects the trading system to take some time to develop and generate interest.

In August, Catex said it had decided to broaden the scope of its system to allow subscribers to trade risks for cash, rather than just swapping risk for risk, making the transactions much more like traditional reinsurance.
At that time, Catex said it expected to begin operations with a 60-90 day trial period in which subscribers could conduct experimental mock trades.
